questions.question: Which white-box coverage criterion additionally requires that all combinations of condition outcomes within a decision be tested?
options: Statement coverage with every executable line exercised once
Data flow coverage
Decision coverage
Multiple condition coverage
questions.explanation: Multiple condition coverage requires testing all possible combinations of individual condition outcomes within a single decision.

questions.question: As a Technical Test Analyst, which type of risk would you PRIMARILY help identify during risk analysis?
options: Organisational risks tied to executive communications and the staffing plans of the department
Technical risks tied to code structure, architecture and non-functional quality
Contractual risks tied to supplier payment terms and legal liabilities
Business risks tied to market positioning and pricing strategy decisions
questions.explanation: Technical Test Analysts bring technical expertise to risk analysis, focusing on architectural, structural, and non-functional risks such as performance, security, and reliability.

questions.question: Which structural coverage criterion requires that every feasible path through a program's control flow graph be exercised?
options: Path coverage
Condition coverage
Statement coverage
Decision coverage
questions.explanation: Path coverage is the strongest and generally most impractical structural coverage criterion, requiring every possible execution path through the code to be exercised.

questions.question: Modified Condition/Decision Coverage (MC/DC) requires that:
options: Every statement in the program is executed at least once by some test
Only the overall decision outcome is exercised as both true and false
Each condition is shown to independently affect the decision outcome
Every combination of condition values in the decision is exercised
questions.explanation: MC/DC requires demonstrating that each condition in a decision can independently affect the decision's outcome, commonly required in safety-critical software standards, without needing full combinatorial testing.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a control-flow-based white-box test technique?
options: Equivalence partitioning of input domains
Checklist-based testing of usability and accessibility heuristics
Use case testing of business scenarios
Statement and decision (branch) coverage testing
questions.explanation: Statement and decision (branch) coverage are control-flow-based white-box techniques that analyze the structure of the code's execution paths.

questions.question: Static analysis tools can be used by Technical Test Analysts to detect which of the following, WITHOUT executing the code?
options: Potential null dereferences, unreachable code and coding-standard violations
Real-time memory consumption observed while the system runs
Failures that appear only when specific inputs are executed
Actual response times measured under realistic production load on a live system
questions.explanation: Static analysis can detect a range of structural and potential defect patterns (e.g. null dereference risks, dead code, coding standard violations) without executing the program.

questions.question: Which technique analyzes how variables are defined, used, and killed throughout a program's execution to design test cases targeting data-related defects?
options: Boundary value analysis
Control flow path testing
State transition testing
Data flow testing
questions.explanation: Data flow testing focuses on sequences of variable definitions and uses (e.g. define-use pairs) to identify tests that can reveal data-related defects, such as using a variable before it's properly defined.

questions.question: Which quality characteristic is PRIMARILY assessed through security testing techniques like penetration testing?
options: Usability
Portability
Security
Functional correctness
questions.explanation: Security testing, including techniques like penetration testing and vulnerability scanning, primarily assesses the security quality characteristic — confidentiality, integrity, and related properties.

questions.question: Reliability testing, such as a soak/endurance test run over 72 hours, primarily aims to detect:
options: Memory leaks, resource exhaustion or gradual loss of stability over time
Missing translations for a specific language or locale
Incorrect wording and grammar in displayed error messages
Cosmetic misalignments of user interface elements and controls on screen
questions.explanation: Reliability (endurance/soak) testing runs the system under sustained load over an extended period to detect issues like memory leaks or gradual resource exhaustion that only appear over time.

questions.question: Which quality characteristic evaluates how easily a system can be modified, extended, or have defects fixed?
options: Portability
Functional suitability
Maintainability
Compatibility
questions.explanation: Maintainability assesses how easily the software can be modified, including corrective, adaptive, and perfective changes, as well as how testable and analyzable the code is.

questions.question: Which activity is MOST closely associated with the Technical Test Analyst's role, as opposed to the Test Analyst's?
options: Deriving test cases purely from user-facing business requirements and workflows
Designing white-box tests from code structure and evaluating non-functional characteristics such as performance and security
Preparing acceptance test scenarios in the language of the business users
Validating that business rules are implemented as the stakeholders expect
questions.explanation: Technical Test Analysts typically focus on structure-based (white-box) testing and technical, non-functional quality characteristics, complementing the Test Analyst's functional/business focus.

questions.question: Which technical factor would typically INCREASE the likelihood component of a risk related to a specific module?
options: No changes to the module for more than two years
Low cyclomatic complexity together with a stable, experienced and well-staffed team
High cyclomatic complexity, a recent rewrite and a history of defects
A clean static analysis report with no warnings in the module
questions.explanation: High complexity, recent significant changes, and a history of defects are technical factors that typically increase the likelihood of a module containing further defects.

questions.question: For the code IF (a) THEN x=1 ELSE IF (b) THEN x=2 ELSE x=3, what is the minimum number of test cases needed to achieve 100% decision coverage?
questions.explanation: The code has two decisions, giving four decision outcomes (a true, a false, b true, b false). They can all be exercised with three tests: a true; a false with b true; a false with b false.

questions.question: Dynamic analysis tools, unlike static analysis tools, detect defects by:
options: Reviewing design documents in a formal inspection meeting
Monitoring the software while it runs, for example to detect memory leaks or wild pointers
Parsing the code to calculate complexity and coupling metrics
Examining the source code for rule violations without executing it
questions.explanation: Dynamic analysis tools operate while the software executes, detecting runtime issues such as memory leaks, wild pointers, or resource usage problems that static analysis cannot observe.

questions.question: Compatibility testing MOST directly evaluates whether a system:
options: Whether it can be moved to a different platform with little effort
Whether it can coexist and interoperate with other software in a shared environment without adverse effects
Whether it resists attempts to access data without authorisation
Whether it runs faster than its previous release under typical load
questions.explanation: Compatibility testing checks that a system can coexist with other software sharing a common environment, without negatively affecting shared resources or functionality.

questions.question: Why might a Technical Test Analyst be involved in code reviews alongside developers?
options: To approve every change request raised against the reviewed code
To contribute a testing view on testability, structural coverage and technical risk
To write the production code on behalf of the development team
To replace the author in deciding which defects must be fixed
questions.explanation: Technical Test Analysts add value in code reviews by focusing on testability, structural risk, and technical concerns that complement the developer's implementation perspective.

questions.question: Condition coverage requires that:
options: Each individual condition is evaluated as both true and false, yet decision coverage is not guaranteed
The overall decision is shown to evaluate to both true and false
Every combination of condition values in the decision is exercised
Every statement is executed at least once, whatever the conditions are
questions.explanation: Condition coverage requires each individual condition to take both true and false values, but on its own does not guarantee that the overall decision outcome has been exercised both ways.

questions.question: Which type of static analysis finding is generally considered a HIGH-value catch because it can cause unpredictable runtime crashes?
options: A possible null pointer dereference or use of an uninitialised variable
A function that has no explanatory header comment above it
A variable name that departs from the team naming convention
A source file whose line length exceeds the formatting guideline agreed by the team
questions.explanation: Static analysis findings like potential null pointer dereferences or uninitialized variable use are high-value because they often correspond to real defects that can cause crashes or undefined behavior.

questions.question: A penetration test discovers that user input is not sanitized before being used in a database query. This is MOST likely evidence of which vulnerability class?
options: Denial of service
Session fixation
Cross-site scripting (XSS)
SQL injection
questions.explanation: Unsanitized user input used directly in database queries is a classic indicator of SQL injection vulnerability, allowing attackers to manipulate queries.

questions.question: Which mitigation approach would a Technical Test Analyst typically recommend for a HIGH technical risk related to a complex, poorly-covered legacy module?
options: Cut the existing tests for the module to free up testing time
Defer attention to the module because it has worked until now
Allow changes to proceed with only the developer's informal checks
Raise structural coverage such as branch coverage and add targeted static and dynamic analysis
questions.explanation: For high-risk, complex, poorly-covered code, a common technical mitigation is to increase structural coverage and apply focused static/dynamic analysis to reduce the residual risk.

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary responsibility of the technical test analyst that differs from the test analyst role?
options: Designing and running tests from internal structure and technical risk, including non-functional testing
Running exploratory sessions against business-facing workflows
Writing acceptance criteria and user stories for business stakeholders
Specifying test conditions from business rules and use cases
questions.explanation: The technical test analyst focuses on structure-based (white-box) testing, technical quality characteristics, and non-functional aspects, which are more code- and architecture-centric than the business-facing test analyst role.

questions.question: From a technical test analyst's perspective, which factor is MOST relevant when assessing the likelihood component of a technical risk?
options: The number of stakeholders who joined the project kick-off
The size of the marketing budget assigned to the feature
The visual design and colour choices of the user interface
Code complexity, technical and organisational factors, and defect history of similar components
questions.explanation: Technical test analysts assess likelihood using factors such as code complexity, technical and organizational factors (e.g., time pressure, team experience), and historical defect data in similar components.

questions.question: How should a technical test analyst adjust the test approach for a component identified as high technical risk?
options: Schedule its testing only after all of the low-risk items are completely finished
Use more rigorous techniques and higher coverage targets, and test it earlier
Release it and rely on production users to find any problems
Reduce its testing because complex parts are hard to test well
questions.explanation: High technical risk components warrant more rigorous test techniques, greater coverage, and earlier test attention to reduce the residual risk before release.

questions.question: What does 'statement coverage' measure in structural testing?
options: The percentage of decision outcomes exercised by the tests
The percentage of requirements covered by at least one executed test case
The percentage of executable statements exercised by the tests
The percentage of reported defects that have been fixed
questions.explanation: Statement coverage measures the percentage of executable statements in the code that have been exercised by the test suite, at least once.

questions.question: Achieving 100% decision coverage guarantees which of the following?
options: Execution of every possible input combination at least once
The absence of remaining defects in the exercised code
100% statement coverage, since every branch taken executes all reachable statements
100% multiple condition coverage, since all outcomes are visited
questions.explanation: 100% decision coverage subsumes 100% statement coverage because every branch (true and false) of every decision is exercised, which necessarily executes every reachable statement, though it does not guarantee all condition combinations or zero defects.

questions.question: Which structural coverage criterion shows the influence of each individual condition on a decision while avoiding the exponential growth in test cases seen with multiple condition coverage?
options: Multiple condition coverage with every outcome combination
Loop coverage
Branch (decision) coverage
Modified Condition/Decision Coverage (MC/DC)
questions.explanation: MC/DC requires that each condition in a decision be shown to independently affect the decision's outcome, achieving strong fault detection with fewer test cases than full multiple condition coverage.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the purpose of data flow testing as a white-box technique?
options: To check that the application complies with accessibility guidelines for impaired users
To follow variables from where a value is defined to where it is used, revealing anomalies such as use of an undefined variable
To confirm that screens and controls are laid out consistently across the user interface
To measure how quickly database queries return results under increasing load
questions.explanation: Data flow testing focuses on the sequences of variable definitions and uses, designing tests that follow paths from where a variable is defined to where it is used, helping reveal data flow anomalies.

questions.question: Why might a technical test analyst prefer branch coverage over pure statement coverage for critical modules?
options: Branch coverage applies to user interface code but not to business logic
Branch coverage can be measured without instrumenting or analysing the source code
Branch coverage generally needs fewer tests than statement coverage for the same piece of code
Branch coverage also demands both outcomes of each decision, giving stronger structural assurance
questions.explanation: Branch (decision) coverage requires that both the true and false outcomes of each decision be exercised, offering stronger fault detection potential than statement coverage alone, especially for critical logic.

questions.question: What is the main goal of static analysis as performed by a technical test analyst?
options: To find defects in code or design without executing the software, for example unreachable code or unused variables
To run the code in a live production environment and observe how real users behave
To calculate the budget variance reported against the project plan at each milestone
To gauge end-user satisfaction with the delivered product through feedback surveys
questions.explanation: Static analysis examines code or design artifacts without executing the software, using tools (or manual review) to detect issues such as unreachable code, unused variables, or violations of coding standards.

questions.question: Cyclomatic complexity is primarily used by a technical test analyst for which purpose?
options: To estimate the number of independent paths through code, which guides how many tests are needed for decision coverage
To judge how appealing the user interface is to the intended audience
To rank features by their commercial priority for the next release
To determine the exact number of defects hidden inside a given module
questions.explanation: Cyclomatic complexity gives the number of linearly independent paths through a module, which technical test analysts use to gauge testing effort; it indicates roughly how many tests full decision coverage may need.

questions.question: Which activity is an example of dynamic analysis, as opposed to static analysis?
options: Inspecting a requirements document for completeness and ambiguity
Reading a test plan carefully before it is approved for use
Checking source code against the coding standard without running the program under test
Spotting memory leaks or wild pointers by observing the program while it executes
questions.explanation: Dynamic analysis involves evaluating a program's behavior while it is executing, such as detecting memory leaks, wild pointers, or resource usage issues at runtime, unlike static analysis which does not execute the code.

questions.question: Which quality characteristic is the technical test analyst primarily responsible for when assessing how easily a system can be modified, extended, or corrected?
options: Functional suitability
Portability
Maintainability
Usability
questions.explanation: Maintainability concerns the ease with which a system can be modified, corrected, or enhanced, and is a key quality focus of the technical test analyst role.

questions.question: Security testing performed by a technical test analyst primarily aims to verify which aspect of the system?
options: That data and systems are protected from unauthorised access, use, disclosure or destruction
That the text on marketing material is free of spelling and grammar errors
That the release notes list every change delivered in the build
That the screens follow the corporate brand and style guidelines
questions.explanation: Security testing evaluates the confidentiality, integrity, authenticity, availability, and non-repudiation of data and systems, verifying protection against unauthorized access, use, disclosure, or destruction.

questions.question: Which of the following is a sub-characteristic of portability that a technical test analyst might test?
options: Learnability, meaning how easily new users can master the system
Adaptability, meaning how well software can be adapted to different environments
Accuracy, meaning whether the outputs produced are correct
Time behaviour, meaning how quickly the system responds when under heavy load
questions.explanation: Adaptability, a sub-characteristic of portability, evaluates how effectively and efficiently a system can be adapted for different or evolving hardware, software, or environmental contexts.

questions.question: Reliability testing performed by a technical test analyst most directly evaluates which of the following?
options: The extent to which the requirements were reviewed by stakeholders
The visual consistency of icons and labels across all screens
The licence and running costs of the tools used for testing
The ability to perform required functions under stated conditions for a specified period without failure
questions.explanation: Reliability testing assesses whether a system can perform its required functions under stated conditions for a specified period without failure, often including sub-characteristics like maturity, availability, and fault tolerance.

questions.question: Which task would a technical test analyst typically perform during test implementation for a structure-based test approach?
options: Approving the overall project scope with the sponsor
Negotiating the contract terms with a third-party supplier
Setting up coverage measurement tools and instrumenting the code under test
Drafting the marketing brochure that announces the release
questions.explanation: Technical test analysts set up and configure tools (such as code coverage tools) needed to measure structural coverage during test implementation for structure-based testing approaches.

questions.question: Which testing technique specifically targets loops in code, checking cases such as zero iterations, one iteration, and the maximum number of iterations?
options: Decision table testing
Pairwise testing
Equivalence partitioning
Loop testing
questions.explanation: Loop testing is a structure-based technique that specifically targets the validity of loop constructs, typically testing boundary conditions such as zero, one, and the maximum number of iterations.

questions.question: In a technical risk assessment, what does 'impact' typically represent?
options: The probability that a defect is present in a given component of the system
The number of test cases needed to cover the component
The consequence or severity of harm if the risk becomes an actual problem
The number of developers assigned to work on the component
questions.explanation: Impact represents the consequence or severity that would result if the risk materialized into an actual problem, and is combined with likelihood to determine overall risk level.

questions.question: Which of these is a typical benefit of using static analysis tools early in development?
options: It finds certain defects, such as unreachable code or undeclared variables, earlier and more cheaply than dynamic testing
It makes formal code reviews unnecessary for the development team
It ensures that the software will pass every later dynamic test
It stands in for version control when tracking source changes
questions.explanation: Static analysis tools can detect certain classes of defects earlier in the lifecycle, before code execution, which is typically cheaper to fix than defects found later via dynamic testing.

questions.question: Compatibility testing, as performed by a technical test analyst, primarily verifies which of the following?
options: That the user manual has been translated into several languages
That the team followed the agreed sprint schedule closely
That the system coexists and shares resources with other systems without harm, and interoperates where needed
That the release notes were approved by the marketing team
questions.explanation: Compatibility testing evaluates whether a system can coexist with other systems sharing a common environment and resources, and interoperate correctly where required, without adversely affecting each other.

questions.question: Which contribution most helps a CI pipeline detect structural regressions in critical code quickly?
options: Adding extra colour themes and widgets to the team dashboard for each release
Merging defect reports into a single summary issued monthly
Running all automated tests once at the end of the release
Publishing coverage and static-analysis trends for the changed module
questions.explanation: Coverage trends and static-analysis results give fast, technical feedback about whether code changes increased structural risk.

questions.question: When developers say a defect cannot be reproduced, which improvement should a Technical Test Analyst usually advocate first?
options: Waiting until production users report the same defect once more
Adding deterministic logging and correlation identifiers around the failing path
Reducing the volume of diagnostic data collected to simplify analysis
Removing the failing assertions so that the test stops reporting the failure to the team
questions.explanation: Deterministic diagnostics make intermittent failures easier to reproduce and isolate without weakening the test.

questions.question: A component hides all state internally and reads the system clock directly. Which redesign most improves its automated technical testability?
options: Retiring the unit tests in favour of manual test scripts
Merging it into neighbouring modules to reduce the call depth and the number of interfaces
Injecting the clock and exposing behaviour through observable interfaces
Adding many more inline comments explaining the time handling
questions.explanation: Injecting time removes nondeterminism, and observable interfaces let tests verify behavior without reaching into implementation details.

questions.question: For an embedded module that depends on a physical sensor not yet available, what is the most useful support for early automated testing?
options: Showing a demonstration of the finished device to the sponsors
Running only final acceptance tests on production hardware
A test driver with a controllable sensor stub or simulator
Postponing all testing until the physical hardware is delivered
questions.explanation: Drivers and simulators let technical tests exercise low-level logic before the real hardware is ready.

questions.question: When choosing a coverage tool for a safety-relevant module, which capability matters most?
options: Offering a built-in chat client so the team can talk
Accurate measurement of the required structural criterion for the target language and build
Producing test reports styled with the company branding
Supporting only the manual execution of test cases
questions.explanation: The tool must measure the required criterion correctly in the actual environment, otherwise coverage evidence is not trustworthy.

questions.question: During an architecture review, which question from a Technical Test Analyst most directly targets testability?
options: Can defect fixes be deferred until after the product goes live?
Can the source be consolidated into fewer files to simplify the build and release process?
Can external failures, timeouts and retries be triggered in a controlled way?
Can the release notes be made shorter and easier to read?
questions.explanation: Controllable failure injection is a strong indicator that fault handling can be tested systematically.

questions.question: A growing backlog of suppressed static-analysis warnings is usually a sign of what?
options: A guarantee that runtime failures cannot occur
A technical debt signal that may be hiding real defects
A healthy sign that technical debt is being reduced
A sign of improved coverage of the business requirements by tests
questions.explanation: Suppressed warnings can normalize risk and make teams less likely to notice important findings.

questions.question: Which handoff artifact is most useful when non-functional automated tests are added to CI?
options: A commitment to look into any failures at a later date
Repeatable execution steps, environment needs and pass/fail thresholds
A screenshot of the final report with no further detail about how it was produced
A list of the people who attended the planning meeting
questions.explanation: CI needs executable, repeatable instructions and clear thresholds so results can be interpreted consistently.

questions.question: A service returns randomized identifiers and timestamps in every response. What should be added to make automated assertions stable?
options: The ability to seed randomness or mask volatile fields in the oracle
A rule to rerun failed tests repeatedly until they eventually pass without changes
Extra manual checkpoints added to each automated test
A reduction in the logging produced by the service
questions.explanation: Stable or normalized outputs are essential so tests fail only for meaningful behavior differences.

questions.question: Which activity best fits a Technical Test Analyst during tool evaluation?
options: Postponing integration checks until after the purchase has been completed
Running a proof of concept on real project code and data
Choosing the tool that generates the longest reports
Picking the tool that has the most attractive icon set
questions.explanation: A proof of concept on realistic artifacts reveals whether the tool provides value in the actual project context.

questions.question: Why might a Technical Test Analyst request extra diagnostic hooks in a highly asynchronous system?
options: To observe event ordering and state transitions when failures occur
To swap all business logging for messages meant only for test runs
To stop developers from reproducing and debugging issues on their machines
To add extra complexity so that the code is harder to reverse-engineer
questions.explanation: Observability is often the key to understanding race conditions and timing-related failures.

questions.question: In a regulated project, why might a simple homegrown harness be rejected for official structural coverage reporting?
options: It may lack the evidence of correctness or qualification needed for trusted measurement
Regulators permit such tools for business analysts but not testers
It tends to overstate the coverage that the tests have achieved
It cannot be combined with automated test execution of any kind
questions.explanation: For regulated evidence, the measurement approach itself may need justification, validation, or qualification.

questions.question: Which code change usually improves automated testing with minimal product risk?
options: Separating pure calculation from input-output side effects
Inlining several unrelated modules into one large function
Replacing meaningful log messages with random identifiers
Removing error codes so that assertions become simpler to write
questions.explanation: Decoupling calculation from side effects makes the logic easier to control and verify in tests.

questions.question: A unit-level performance test is noisy because it runs on a shared machine. What should the Technical Test Analyst do first?
options: Stabilise the environment and define a repeatable measurement protocol
Convert the test to manual execution and record results by hand
Delete the test, since automated tools cannot measure performance reliably
Raise the threshold until the test passes on every noisy run
questions.explanation: Controlling measurement conditions is necessary before the numbers can support technical decisions.

questions.question: Which automation smell most undermines trust in technical tests?
options: Intermittent failures that are unrelated to product changes
Tests that execute in parallel across several machines
Tests that write detailed logs for every step they perform
Tests that run faster after an optimisation of the test code
questions.explanation: Flaky tests erode confidence because teams cannot tell whether a failure indicates a product defect or test instability.

questions.question: When a new static-analysis tool is introduced, which responsibility most naturally fits the Technical Test Analyst?
options: Tuning rules and thresholds together with developers, based on risk
Retiring all existing review practices once the new tool is running in the team
Owning the payroll calculations produced for the project team
Approving changes to the product's branding and visual identity
questions.explanation: The Technical Test Analyst helps align tool findings with technical risk so teams focus on high-value checks.

questions.question: A team insists that every defect must be reproduced manually before it may be automated. What is the strongest technical objection?
options: Manual reproduction is slow and hard to repeat, while automation preserves the exact conditions
Manual execution gives better structural coverage than automated runs do
Automated tests are unable to examine technical behaviour of a system
Manual reproduction is nearly always faster than writing an automated test
questions.explanation: Encoding the reproduction as automation preserves the conditions that exposed the defect and reduces future diagnosis effort.

questions.question: For a multi-service test environment, which design choice best helps isolate a suspected interface defect?
options: Sending all test traffic through the live production services instead
Writing more end-user manuals for each of the services
Randomising the order in which all the services start up
Virtualising service boundaries with controllable responses
questions.explanation: Controllable boundary behavior helps the team prove whether the failure originates in the caller, callee, or the contract between them.

questions.question: Which trend would most interest a Technical Test Analyst reviewing code quality over time?
options: Growing complexity and duplicated logic in frequently changed code
A decline in the number of calendar invites and status meetings sent to the team
A rising count of emojis used in commit messages
An expanding list of public holidays on the company calendar
questions.explanation: Growing complexity and duplication raise technical risk because they increase the chance that changes introduce defects.

questions.question: When reviewing an API meant for fault-injection tests, which feature is most useful?
options: Explicit timeouts and configurable failure responses
A colourful logo displayed on the generated OpenAPI page
A policy that bans negative test cases against the interface
A rule that each response must contain randomised content
questions.explanation: Fault-injection testing depends on being able to provoke and observe controlled failure scenarios.

questions.question: A team tracks only end-to-end pass rate and ignores low-level coverage and tool findings. What risk remains?
options: No extra diagnostic effort will be needed at any later stage
Complete path coverage is gained automatically by the passing system tests of the product
Critical structural blind spots can stay hidden behind passing system tests
Technical debt is reduced by definition as pass rates climb
questions.explanation: System tests can miss risky branches, error handlers, and data-flow problems that technical evidence would reveal.

questions.question: Which task is a good example of technical test support for maintainability?
options: Replacing automated tests with manually maintained spreadsheets
Building reusable test data builders and helpers
Renaming the product for marketing reasons before release
Deleting shared utilities so each test re-implements its own
questions.explanation: Reusable technical test assets lower maintenance cost and make future regression suites easier to extend.

questions.question: Which component should usually receive the earliest technical risk attention?
options: A slide deck that explains the product roadmap to staff
An archived prototype that is no longer part of the release and receives no changes
A shared authentication library used by every customer-facing service
A static help page that contains no executable logic
questions.explanation: A defect in a shared critical library can affect many services, so both impact and exposure are high.

questions.question: Why does missing observability raise technical risk in a distributed workflow?
options: Regression testing becomes unnecessary for later changes
The user interface appears simpler to the people using it
Failures are harder to detect, localise and diagnose
System performance improves under heavy load as a side effect
questions.explanation: Poor observability increases the chance that important failures escape or take too long to investigate.

questions.question: A new payment scheduler introduces concurrency control around account updates. Why is this often ranked as high technical risk?
options: Concurrency control eliminates every state-related defect in updates
Scheduling code is exempt from structure-based test techniques
Rare timing faults are hard to trigger, diagnose and contain, and the impact is financial
The feature is expected to attract very few users after launch
questions.explanation: Concurrency defects are often intermittent and high-impact, especially when they affect financial consistency.

questions.question: In technical risk analysis, what does impact describe?
options: Whether the code formatter changes the indentation style
How many developers favour working on the component
The number of meetings that are scheduled during the sprint
The damage or loss that results if the failure occurs
questions.explanation: Impact reflects the consequence of failure, not how much effort the team expects to spend testing.

questions.question: A third-party package has a recently disclosed critical vulnerability. What should the Technical Test Analyst note immediately?
options: Risk exists only if the team modified the package source
The package can no longer influence release decisions
Exposure may be high even though no local code changed
Only usability testing needs to be adjusted in response
questions.explanation: Inherited vulnerabilities can create major technical risk even when the application code itself did not change.

questions.question: Which situation most increases the likelihood component of technical risk?
options: A read-only configuration file that has no runtime behaviour
A recently rewritten, complex module owned by an inexperienced team
A stable module with simple logic, broad regression coverage and few recent changes
A library that is unchanged for years and shows few defects
questions.explanation: Complexity, recent change, and low team familiarity combine to increase the chance of latent defects.

questions.question: A legacy parser has frequent production fixes but almost no automated tests. What is the best first mitigation?
options: Add focused characterisation and structural tests around defect-prone paths
Hold off on testing until funding for a full rewrite exists
Drop the parser from all regression plans to save time
Depend on product demonstrations given by the marketing team to show the parser works
questions.explanation: Targeted tests can quickly reduce risk by locking down current behavior and exercising risky branches.

questions.question: Which artifact most helps identify how a failing component could affect neighboring components?
options: A list of the desk locations across the office floor
An architecture or interface dependency diagram
The colour palette defined for the product's interface
The schedule for team lunches during the project
questions.explanation: Dependency information helps the Technical Test Analyst estimate blast radius and prioritize integration checks.

questions.question: An internet-facing file upload service uses a custom parser for untrusted content. Which test emphasis is most appropriate?
options: Skipping negative tests because the files come from users
Targeted robustness, security and structural tests on parsing and error handling
Confirming that the landing page loads after each deployment
Happy-path checks driven through the user interface alone
questions.explanation: Custom parsing of untrusted input is a classic high-risk area that merits deep negative and structural testing.

questions.question: Which change would usually lower the likelihood of technical failure in a module?
options: Introducing additional hidden global state into the module to share data between callers
Raising the change frequency while skipping code review
Keeping the module small and stable, with good automated test coverage
Stripping diagnostics out of the failure-handling paths
questions.explanation: Small stable modules with good automation give fewer opportunities for defects to be introduced and missed.

questions.question: Why does high change frequency matter in technical risk assessment?
options: Frequent edits raise the chance of introducing new defects
It ensures that defects are always found at an earlier point
It mainly affects office planning rather than software risk
It removes the need for regression testing of the module
questions.explanation: Even simple code becomes riskier when it changes often because prior evidence may no longer reflect the current state.

questions.question: Two modules would cause similar damage if they failed, but one has complex threading and past deadlocks. How should it be ranked?
options: Higher, because its likelihood is greater even though the impact is similar
Lower, because concurrency problems are mostly theoretical
Equal, because only the size of the impact matters when the two modules are ranked
Unranked, because past technical history should be ignored
questions.explanation: Risk ranking depends on both impact and likelihood; a history of concurrency defects raises the likelihood.

questions.question: What does repeated defect clustering in one subsystem suggest?
options: The subsystem no longer needs any further testing effort
Architectural dependencies of the subsystem can be disregarded
The test team is the origin of the defects that were found
Similar latent faults may well remain in that same area
questions.explanation: Defect clustering is a practical signal that more faults may be concentrated in the same area.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects how exposure is commonly prioritized in risk-based testing?
options: By combining likelihood and impact instead of relying on effort alone
By the age of the comments found in the source code
By the headcount of the team that is deploying the release
By the amount of execution time that each test is expected to take on average
questions.explanation: Risk-based prioritization focuses on where failure is both likely and damaging.

questions.question: For a performance-sensitive transaction path, what is the best risk-based action before full regression begins?
options: Swap the automated tests for manual stopwatch timing of steps
Track only the average sprint velocity of the development team
Leave performance checks until the final week before release
Run early, targeted load profiling on the critical path
questions.explanation: Early technical evidence on the critical path can reveal serious performance risks while there is still time to respond.

questions.question: Why might exit criteria be stricter for a high technical risk area than for a low-risk utility?
options: Exit criteria must be set identically for every single component
Low-risk utilities are exempt from any testing whatsoever
Strict criteria are applied mainly to satisfy documentation needs of the project office
Higher-risk areas need stronger evidence that the residual risk is acceptable
questions.explanation: Stricter evidence is justified where failure consequences or likelihood are higher.

questions.question: Which item deserves higher priority in a risk discussion?
options: A source comment that runs past the preferred line length
A cosmetic typo that appears often in the debug logs
A test report that still carries outdated company branding
A rare crash that can corrupt customer data
questions.explanation: A low-frequency but catastrophic failure can outrank common minor issues because the impact is much greater.

questions.question: How should static-analysis findings influence technical risk assessment?
options: They become relevant only after the product has been released and users report problems
They should be set aside until system testing has failed
They can sharpen hotspot identification and drive deeper targeted testing
They remove any need for testing the software at runtime
questions.explanation: Findings such as dangerous APIs, null-dereference risks, or complexity spikes help focus testing where technical risk is higher.

questions.question: Why is an undocumented algorithm delivered by an external contractor often considered riskier?
options: Externally written code is fixed and is never modified later
Knowledge gaps make review, maintenance and defect diagnosis harder
Documentation has little bearing on the technical risk of a component
Code written by contractors cannot be tested with standard techniques
questions.explanation: When design intent is unclear, the team has less basis for review, impact analysis, and precise testing.

questions.question: An autoscaling defect can launch many unnecessary instances under load. Why is its impact often rated high?
options: It stops other defects from occurring in the same service
It touches only cosmetic monitoring metrics on dashboards
It lessens the need for monitoring of the running platform
It can cause severe cost growth and destabilise the platform at peak traffic
questions.explanation: Autoscaling faults can amplify operational impact quickly by wasting resources or destabilizing service behavior.

questions.question: Hard-coded secrets are found in deployment automation. Why is this usually a high technical risk?
options: Compromise can spread widely and may be easy to exploit
They matter only once the next hardware refresh takes place
They speed up deployment by an unacceptably large amount
They influence only the formatting of the automation scripts
questions.explanation: Exposed secrets can enable widespread unauthorized access, making both likelihood and impact serious.

questions.question: After adding mitigations for a risky component, what should the Technical Test Analyst still communicate?
options: The residual risk and any untested assumptions that remain
That testing is now finished and nothing further needs to be explained to stakeholders
That further risk discussions are no longer required
That the mitigations ensure the component has zero defects
questions.explanation: Risk rarely drops to zero, so stakeholders still need to understand what uncertainty remains.

questions.question: To achieve decision coverage for a simple if-else statement, what must the tests do?
options: Run only the longest branch of the statement in each test
Use each possible input value for the controlling variable
Exercise both the true and false outcomes of the decision
Execute every statement in alphabetical order of its label
questions.explanation: Decision coverage requires each decision outcome to be taken at least once.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes condition coverage?
options: Only the proportion of statements that executed is measured
Short-circuit evaluation of conditions is taken into account
Each atomic condition in a decision evaluates to both true and false at least once
Every feasible path through the code has been executed
questions.explanation: Condition coverage is concerned with the truth values of the individual conditions that form a decision.

questions.question: A decision contains three independent boolean conditions. How many combinations are required for full multiple condition coverage?
questions.explanation: Multiple condition coverage requires all true-false combinations, which for three conditions is 2^3 = 8.

questions.question: Why is MC-DC often chosen instead of full multiple condition coverage for critical logic?
options: It disregards the overall decision result completely
It can be satisfied without running the code at all
It is a weaker criterion than statement coverage
It gives strong evidence that each condition matters, using fewer tests
questions.explanation: MC-DC keeps strong fault-detection power while avoiding the full combinatorial explosion of multiple condition coverage.

questions.question: If one control-flow path is infeasible because its conditions can never be satisfied together, what does that mean for path coverage?
options: Only feasible paths are candidates for complete path coverage
The infeasible path must still be forced with special test data
Every path coverage goal has to be dropped for the code
Decision coverage can no longer be achieved for the code
questions.explanation: Structural criteria are interpreted against feasible behavior; infeasible paths should be justified, not artificially executed.

questions.question: Cyclomatic complexity of 6 implies what for basis path testing?
options: No more than 6 test cases may be written for the code
At least 6 statements have to be executed by the tests
The code already has full decision coverage by definition of the metric
There are 6 linearly independent paths to consider as a baseline
questions.explanation: Cyclomatic complexity approximates the number of linearly independent paths that should be considered for basis path coverage.

questions.question: What is an LCSAJ in structural testing?
options: A linear sequence of code followed by a jump
A checklist used during user acceptance
A listing of load and stress measurements taken during a test
A snapshot of dynamic memory contents
questions.explanation: An LCSAJ is a low-level structural unit consisting of straight-line code and the jump that ends it.

questions.question: In data flow testing, what is a def-use pair?
options: A decision together with the return statement that follows it
Any two statements that appear next to each other in the code
Two different variables that are assigned in a single block
A variable definition and a later use reachable with no redefinition in between
questions.explanation: Data flow testing tracks how defined values travel to later uses along specific paths.

questions.question: Why does loop testing pay special attention to zero, one, and boundary iteration counts?
options: Decision coverage takes no account of loop constructs
A loop can be exercised with only a single input value
Loop variables carry no risk and need no attention
Initialisation and off-by-one defects often appear near iteration boundaries
questions.explanation: Boundary iteration counts are where setup, termination, and limit logic often fail.

questions.question: For nested loops, what is a common starting strategy?
options: Omit the inner loop, because the outer loop already covers it in every test that is run
Choose iteration counts at random for all of the loops
Exercise inner-loop boundaries while keeping outer loops at simple values
Set every loop to its maximum count from the very first test
questions.explanation: Controlling one loop at a time makes it easier to isolate defects in nested iteration logic.

questions.question: Why should exception handlers be included in branch coverage analysis?
options: They are counted only towards statement coverage
They cannot be triggered while the tests are running
They are documentation only and carry no executable behaviour that needs exercising
They are alternate control-flow outcomes with logic of their own
questions.explanation: Catch, fallback, and cleanup paths often contain unique behavior that must be exercised explicitly.

questions.question: When API tests are designed from server-side code structure, what is the main structural focus?
options: The size of the backend development team
The look and branding of the API developer portal
The alphabetical ordering and naming of the exposed endpoints in the portal
Branches for validation, authorisation and error mapping
questions.explanation: Code-aware API testing targets distinct internal paths such as validation branches and exception mapping logic.

questions.question: A test suite reaches 100% statement coverage. What can still be missing?
options: Execution of the false outcome of some decisions
Compilation of the program under test into a build
Execution of every statement at least once by some test
The availability of an environment to run the tests in
questions.explanation: Statement coverage can miss untested decision outcomes when the executed statements overlap.

questions.question: In a control-flow graph, what do edges usually represent?
options: Transfers of control between nodes
Lines of comments in the source file
Data values supplied to the tests
Priorities assigned to defects found
questions.explanation: Edges connect the program points that execution can move between.

questions.question: What extra structural concern applies when white-box testing a recursive function?
options: Only the deepest possible call stack needs to be examined
Recursive code cannot be drawn as a control-flow graph
Recursion makes branch coverage unnecessary for the function
Both the base case and recursive progress toward termination must be exercised
questions.explanation: Recursive logic is safe only when tests show both entry into recursion and proper termination behavior.

questions.question: Condition coverage is mainly concerned with what?
options: The number of requirements linked to the code
Whether the code contains enough explanatory comments for the maintainers to follow it
Each atomic condition taking both true and false values
Only the final outcome of the decision
questions.explanation: Condition coverage focuses on the individual boolean parts that build a decision.

questions.question: A variable is assigned in one branch and later used after branches merge. What should data flow testing pay attention to?
options: Whether the point where the branches merge sits inside a loop
The colour used to draw each branch in the flow diagram
Definition-use paths through the different branches
Whether each variable name is descriptive enough to follow
questions.explanation: Different branches may define or skip values differently, so the downstream use deserves targeted def-use checks.

questions.question: Why can unreachable code complicate interpretation of structural coverage goals?
options: It has an effect on usability testing but not on structural testing
Unreachable code is counted automatically as covered code
Coverage tools are unable to read the source files at all
The measured denominator may include code that cannot execute until it is removed or justified
questions.explanation: Teams should distinguish missed coverage from code that truly has no executable path.

questions.question: Which loop-focused test is especially good at exposing initialization mistakes?
options: A test that skips all of the set-up code
A test that uses only an average input size
A test that runs with its assertions disabled to speed up the execution
A test in which the loop body executes zero times
questions.explanation: Zero-iteration execution checks whether the code behaves correctly before the first pass ever occurs.

questions.question: Why does short-circuit evaluation matter in structural testing of compound decisions?
options: It means decisions no longer produce boolean values
Some conditions might not be evaluated on every execution of the decision
It makes branch coverage impossible to measure for the code that contains such decisions
It alters only how the source code is formatted
questions.explanation: With short-circuit logic, tests must be chosen carefully if each condition is expected to be exercised.

questions.question: In LCSAJ testing, what distinguishes two LCSAJs that share the same straight-line sequence?
options: Their different jump targets or end points
How recently the code was written
The indentation style and line-wrapping conventions used in the code
The count of comments inside the block
questions.explanation: The terminating jump is part of the structural unit, so different exits define different LCSAJs.

questions.question: Why is complete path coverage rarely practical in real systems?
options: Coverage tools refuse to count paths in any program
Loops, recursion and combined decisions cause an explosion in the number of paths
Path coverage is a weaker criterion than statement coverage
Real systems contain no branching logic to cover
questions.explanation: Even modest control flow can create too many paths to enumerate and execute exhaustively.

questions.question: What does a static-analysis dead-store warning usually mean?
options: A database row was removed unexpectedly while the program was running in production
A value is assigned but never read before it is overwritten or discarded
The program ran out of disk space while it was running
A variable name is shorter than the style guide allows
questions.explanation: Dead stores often indicate redundant logic or a missing intended use of the assigned value.

questions.question: Cyclomatic complexity is most useful for estimating what?
options: The number of independent paths to consider and the relative effort for review
The amount of RAM the software consumes while running
The total number of user stories planned for a release
The likelihood that a security attack will be attempted
questions.explanation: Higher complexity suggests more decision logic and usually more structural paths that deserve attention.

questions.question: How can a call graph help when a risky shared utility is modified?
options: It shows that no regression testing is required after the shared utility changes
It takes the place of reviewing the changed source code
It detects memory leaks in the utility automatically
It reveals direct and indirect callers that may need focused retesting
questions.explanation: Impact analysis is stronger when the team can see which code paths depend on the changed utility.

questions.question: Code located after an unconditional return statement is typically classified as what?
options: Unreachable code
A performance hotspot
Thread contention
A test stub
questions.explanation: If control cannot reach the statements, static analysis will often report them as unreachable or dead code.

questions.question: Which data-flow anomaly is indicated when a variable is defined and then redefined without any use in between?
options: A suspicious redundant-assignment pattern
A case that loop coverage requires to be exercised
A normal def-use pair that needs no attention
Certain memory corruption in the running program
questions.explanation: Redefinition before use may mean the first assignment is pointless or the intended use was skipped.

questions.question: During an endurance run, memory consumption rises steadily while workload stays constant. What does this most strongly suggest?
options: A block of dead commented-out code
Improved portability of the software across different platforms
Higher branch coverage in the code
A memory leak or retained-object problem
questions.explanation: If work stays stable but memory does not, the software is likely failing to release or reuse objects correctly.

questions.question: What is a wild pointer or invalid reference?
options: A pointer used inside a white-box coverage tool
A branch whose condition always evaluates to true during every test execution
A reference pointing to unpredictable or illegal memory
A counter that reports CPU usage over time
questions.explanation: Wild pointers can cause crashes or silent corruption because the program no longer controls what the reference targets.

questions.question: A profiler shows that 70% of execution time is spent serializing JSON. What is the best interpretation?
options: Only the network layer deserves any further testing
The profiler is faulty, as one function cannot dominate runtime
The application has already achieved complete path coverage
JSON serialisation is a performance hotspot worth investigating
questions.explanation: Profilers help the team focus optimization and measurement effort on the code that actually consumes time.

questions.question: Which type of runtime tool is most suitable for diagnosing lock contention and deadlocks?
options: A screenshot comparison tool
A concurrency or thread analyser
A spell checker run over the source
A static naming-rule checker
questions.explanation: Thread analyzers observe blocking behavior and synchronization problems while the program runs.

questions.question: A recursive algorithm fails only with very large input sizes. Which runtime symptom should be investigated first?
options: An outdated label on the issue tracker
Stack exhaustion caused by deep recursion
A missing project logo and branding assets on the start page
A low level of statement coverage
questions.explanation: Large recursion depth commonly manifests as stack overflow or exhaustion at runtime.

questions.question: In a technical review of numeric code, which checklist item is especially valuable?
options: Whether the team prefers tabs or spaces for indentation
Possible overflow, underflow and loss of precision
Whether the code has enough blank lines in it
Whether variable names are in alphabetical order
questions.explanation: Numeric defects often appear at range limits or due to precision assumptions that are easy to overlook.

questions.question: If a static analyzer produces too many false positives, what is the best response?
options: Treat each reported warning as a confirmed defect
Tune rules and baselines so that high-value findings stay visible
Run the analyser only against the production system once the release has been deployed
Switch the analysis off permanently for the project
questions.explanation: Well-tuned analysis keeps important warnings actionable without drowning the team in noise.

questions.question: Why is clone detection useful to a Technical Test Analyst?
options: It ensures that the code runs faster at runtime
It takes the place of code reviews in the process
Duplicated logic can widen regression scope and repeat the same defects
It measures compatibility with different browsers
questions.explanation: When the same logic exists in many places, a defect and its fix may need attention in each copy.

questions.question: Why are runtime sanitizers valuable in C or C++ testing?
options: They take the place of all design reviews
They can catch invalid memory accesses during execution, with context
They automatically demonstrate portability of the code to every supported platform
They improve how screens are laid out for users
questions.explanation: Sanitizers instrument execution to reveal faults such as buffer overruns and use-after-free errors.

questions.question: How can heap snapshots taken before and after a long test run help diagnosis?
options: They remove the need to generate load for the test
They demonstrate that the code is free of race conditions and deadlocks
They report the statement coverage that was achieved
They show which objects were unexpectedly retained over time
questions.explanation: Comparing snapshots is a common way to find classes or object graphs that keep accumulating.

questions.question: In an interface-focused technical review, which question best supports robustness testing?
options: How many team meetings were held in the last month?
How are invalid inputs, timeouts and partial failures reported to callers?
Should negative tests be forbidden for the interface?
Which background image does the API team prefer to use?
questions.explanation: Robustness depends on how clearly and consistently the interface behaves under abnormal conditions.

questions.question: Why is taint analysis useful in technical testing?
options: It traces untrusted data flowing toward sensitive operations
It measures how much CPU time a loop consumes
It entirely replaces penetration testing activities carried out by security specialists
It counts the LCSAJs in the code automatically
questions.explanation: Tracing risky data flows can reveal injection paths and unsafe trust boundaries before runtime.

questions.question: Why does a high fan-in utility deserve careful review after a change?
options: High fan-in means that the code contains no branches
It can be tested only through manual test execution
A defect can affect many dependent paths, widening the blast radius
Utilities that have many callers are always slower than other kinds of code in the system
questions.explanation: Call concentration is important because one small change can have many indirect consequences.

questions.question: Which trend often signals rising maintainability risk in code metrics?
options: A steady number of test accounts being maintained in the shared test environments
More hardware being installed in the office
Complexity and function length growing release after release
Fewer archived chat messages in the team channel
questions.explanation: Growing complexity is a practical early warning that understanding and changing the code will get harder.

questions.question: A benchmark's first iteration is much slower because caches and JIT compilation are cold. What is the best practice?
options: Report only the slowest run to stay on the cautious side
Discard every measurement taken after the first iteration
Separate warm-up from steady-state measurements
Switch off test automation for the performance tests
questions.explanation: Warm-up effects should be controlled so performance conclusions reflect stable runtime behavior.

questions.question: Why are use-after-free defects often difficult to reproduce consistently?
options: They occur solely within sections of commented-out code
They can depend on timing and memory-reuse patterns at runtime
They vanish whenever the tests are executed a second time under identical settings
Statement coverage on its own is enough to detect them
questions.explanation: Once memory has been released, whether the fault appears can vary with allocator behavior and execution timing.

questions.question: If review capacity is limited, which modules should be prioritized for deep technical review?
options: Modules that are owned by the largest team
Modules that compile faster than the others
Modules with high complexity, recent change and a history of defects
Modules that have the most colourful dashboards
questions.explanation: Combining multiple risk indicators helps technical review effort go where it is most likely to pay off.

questions.question: Running the same product on Windows, Linux, and macOS without code changes primarily examines which quality characteristic?
options: Reviewability
Portability
Functional completeness
Marketability
questions.explanation: Portability is concerned with how well software can be transferred or adapted across environments.

questions.question: What should installability testing verify most directly?
options: That user stories have been estimated accurately by the team during planning sessions
That the source code has a low level of complexity
That each API in the product returns its data as JSON
That install, upgrade and uninstall work properly and recover from failures
questions.explanation: Installability includes successful setup and safe handling of failures during installation or upgrade.

questions.question: Two systems exchange the same numeric field but one interprets it as seconds and the other as milliseconds. What kind of issue is this?
options: A gap in statement coverage of the code
A successful result for portability testing
A purely maintainability issue in the code
An interoperability defect
questions.explanation: Both systems can communicate syntactically yet still fail to interoperate semantically.

questions.question: What does coexistence testing mainly check?
options: Whether the product can share resources with other software without unacceptable interference
Whether each branch in the code has been covered by tests
Whether all code comments have been translated
Whether developers agree on naming conventions in the code
questions.explanation: Coexistence is about peacefully sharing an environment such as CPU, memory, network, or file handles.

questions.question: After a database restart, a service resumes queued work without losing committed data. Which reliability aspect is being demonstrated?
options: Installability
Confidentiality
Replaceability
Recoverability
questions.explanation: Recoverability concerns how well the system restores service and data after an interruption.

questions.question: Which change would most improve analyzability from a maintainability perspective?
options: Hiding errors behind one generic success message that is shown to every caller
Adding structured diagnostics and clear module boundaries
Packing more behaviour into a single long method
Replacing log text with random numeric codes
questions.explanation: Good diagnostics and modular structure make faults easier to understand, trace, and fix.

questions.question: Using a least-privilege service account mainly supports which security objective?
options: Lowering the coverage targets that apply to the code in the account's scope
Limiting the damage if the account is compromised
Making on-screen text easier to read
Removing the need to take backups
questions.explanation: Least privilege reduces the blast radius of misuse or compromise.

questions.question: Time-behavior testing is primarily concerned with what?
options: Whether the installer displays the company logo
How frequently the code comments get updated
How many risk workshops were scheduled in the project
Response times and throughput under stated conditions
questions.explanation: Time behavior focuses on how quickly the system responds and how much work it can process.

questions.question: Encrypting stored files most directly protects which security property?
options: Replaceability
Modularity
Availability of the stored data
Confidentiality
questions.explanation: Encryption mainly helps prevent unauthorized disclosure of the data contents.

questions.question: Why does modularity usually improve maintainability?
options: It removes the need for tests of the code
It makes all performance problems disappear
Changes can be localised rather than spreading across unrelated areas
It ensures the code contains no defects at all
questions.explanation: Well-defined modules reduce ripple effects and make understanding and changing the code easier.

questions.question: Swapping one database driver for another through the same standard interface primarily demonstrates which sub-characteristic?
options: Fault tolerance
Replaceability
Suitability
Authenticity
questions.explanation: Replaceability is about using one product element in place of another for the same purpose.

questions.question: A service continues in degraded mode during a network partition and synchronizes later. Which reliability aspect is most evident?
options: Compatibility branding
Statement coverage
Fault tolerance
Installability
questions.explanation: Fault tolerance is the ability to continue providing acceptable service despite certain faults.

questions.question: Why are predictable session identifiers a serious security weakness?
options: They increase the size of the backups taken
Attackers may guess valid identifiers and hijack sessions
They reduce the compiler's ability to optimise the generated code
They lower the branch coverage that tests can reach
questions.explanation: Predictable identifiers can let an attacker impersonate users by anticipating future session values.

questions.question: Resource-utilization testing is intended to answer which question?
options: Whether the help pages are written in clear language
Whether code reviews have enough participants
Whether CPU, memory and I/O stay within acceptable limits under load
Whether every requirement carries a unique identifier in the tracking tool used by the team
questions.explanation: Resource utilization looks at how efficiently the system consumes shared resources while doing its work.

questions.question: Two applications work correctly alone, but together one starves the other's disk bandwidth. What quality issue does this reveal?
options: A portability success
A coexistence problem
A replaceability problem
A dead-store warning
questions.explanation: The problem appears only when the software shares its environment with other software, which is exactly what coexistence addresses.

questions.question: Opening files created by an older tool version with the current tool most directly tests what?
options: Interoperability or backward compatibility of exchanged artefacts
Cyclomatic complexity of the tool
Loop coverage achieved by the tests
Heap usage of the running tool
questions.explanation: If exchanged artifacts remain usable across versions or tools, compatibility has improved.

questions.question: An application fails only on a case-sensitive file system because it mixes file-name casing. Which characteristic is most directly affected?
options: Security
Portability
Usability
Functional completeness
questions.explanation: Hidden assumptions about the platform often surface as portability problems across environments.

questions.question: What maintainability problem is most directly indicated by duplicated validation rules scattered across several services?
options: Guaranteed replaceability of each service
Better confidentiality of the data handled
Poor modifiability, since changes must be made consistently in several places
Improved analysability of the validation logic
questions.explanation: Scattered duplication increases the chance that future changes will be incomplete or inconsistent.

questions.question: Restarting a process from a checkpoint after a crash primarily checks which reliability aspect?
options: Recoverability
Interoperability
Code style
Compatibility
questions.explanation: Checkpoint restart is a direct way to evaluate how well service can be restored after failure.

questions.question: When old clients and new servers continue working through API version negotiation, which characteristic is most directly shown?
options: Installability
Interoperability
Replaceability
Cyclomatic simplicity
questions.explanation: Version negotiation is a common technique for keeping independently evolving systems interoperable.

questions.question: Why is the ability to bypass rate limits with parallel requests a serious security defect?
options: It affects portability of the service but nothing else
It mainly affects how text is formatted in responses
It weakens protection against abuse and can enable denial-of-service or brute-force attacks
It improves the fairness of throughput across clients
questions.explanation: Rate limiting is a defensive control; bypassing it can make abuse easier and magnify attack impact.

questions.question: Why should a portable native library be tested on 32-bit and 64-bit platforms with different data-model assumptions?
options: Portability work excludes the use of automated tests
Branch coverage is defined separately for each CPU architecture and must be measured on each one
Hidden assumptions about type size, alignment or representation may break
Dynamic analysis tools do not exist on one of the platforms
questions.explanation: Cross-platform issues often appear when code assumes a specific integer width, pointer size, or memory layout.
